title: ECM protein expression changes in FAK-expressing and FAK-deficient MOVCAR model
projectDescription: Data-independent acquisition (DIA) mass spectrometry was used to study the collagen and matrisome protein expression between FAK-expressing and FAK-deficient mouse ovarian carcinoma (MOVCAR) models
sampleProcessingProtocol: Murine ovarian cancer 99A cell lines (99A_FAK_WT_AA, 99A_FAK_WT_INH, 99A_FAK_KO_GFP_AA) and tumour tissue samples (T241, T223) were decellularised, followed by reduction and alkylation. The proteins were digested in S-Trap microcolumn with Trypsin/Lys-C. The digested peptides were desalted using C18 tips and then injected into Q Exactive HF Orbitrap mass spectrometer. The peptide mixtures were separated with mobile phase buffer A (0.1% formic acid) and B (acetonitrile/water (95:5(v/v)), over a 50-minute gradient (8–35% B in 40 min, 35-100% B in 2 min and held at 100% B for 8 min). Data acquisition was performed with DIA mode, in which each cycle of full scan of 366-1007 m/z at a resolution of 120,000 was performed. DIA MS2 scans at a resolution of 30,000 were performed for all DIA scans with 40 fixed windows (17 m/z) overlapped by 1 m/z.
dataProcessingProtocol: The DIA data were processed using Spectronaut (version 16.0.220606.53000, Biognosys) using directDIA workflow, searched against a mouse FASTA database containing reviewed and unreviewed sequences of UniprotKB release 2022_03. Carbamidomethyl (C) as fixed modification, while oxidation (M, P, K) and N-terminal protein acetylation were set as variable modifications. A maximum of 5 variable modifications was allowed with a peptide length of 7-52 amino acids. Precursors were filtered based on Q values, and the quantification was based on MS2 data, which were then log2 transformed, followed by minimum value imputation and median normalisation.
